product: Designs, manufactures and distributes regulated land-based electronic gaming machines, cabinets and casino management systems, free-to-play social casino mobile games under Product Madness, and regulated online real-money gaming plus iLottery content, platforms and services under Aristocrat Interactive.
demand: Demand is driven by casino floor replacement and expansion cycles, state lottery and iLottery adoption, and mobile social-casino engagement. HY26 showed rising installed-base share and recurring revenue, though FY26 group revenue is modelled down on FX and portfolio effects.
pricing_power: Strong and rising. Record Gaming profitability with 43 percent North American installed-base share and royalty-bearing patent licensing to Ainsworth indicate pricing and IP leverage, though competition and operator budgets cap how far it can be pushed.
competition: Light and Wonder, IGT, Konami and Ainsworth in land-based; SciPlay and PlayStudios in social casino; Playtech and Evolution in online content. Aristocrat resolved its Light and Wonder litigation in January 2026 and now licenses patents to Ainsworth.
team: CEO and Managing Director Trevor Croker has led since March 2017; Matthew Primmer is Chief Product Officer; the board added Michael Rumbolz on 4 August 2026; roughly 7,300 to 7,400 employees. CFO and Interactive leadership were refreshed in 2025 and 2026.
market_strategy: Grow share in land-based Gaming, scale Aristocrat Interactive toward a US 1B dollar FY29 revenue target via iLottery, content and platforms, sustain Product Madness, invest in design, development and AI, and return capital through dividends and buy-backs.
bull: HY26 revenue AUD 3.03B up 6.4% constant currency on volume and mix; North America installed share 43%, ANZ units nearly doubled, iLottery live in MA and MI, royalty patent licence to Ainsworth, buy-backs ongoing.
bear: FY26 consensus revenue down 2.57% to AUD 6.14B and net income lower YoY; stock AUD 58.40, down 2.49% on 2026-09-25 and ~18% below 52-week high; ~24.6x earnings with fair value 52.05.
falsifier: FY26 results on 2026-11-12 show group revenue decline and NPATA below FY25, or the US 1B dollar FY29 Interactive target is cut.
web_what_changed: 90 days to 2026-09-25: FY26 results scheduled 2026-11-12; Jul 1 2026 Investor Briefing; Aug 4 2026 Michael Rumbolz appointed director; Aug 14 2026 royalty-bearing Hold and Spin patent licence granted to Ainsworth; Aug 10 2026 new cabinet launch; Jul 2026 iLottery launches for Massachusetts and Michigan plus Lightning Link online. Daily buy-backs continued after the May 13 2026 AUD 1B buy-back expansion.
web_not_known_yesterday: Nothing material. Only routine ASX buy-back update notices dated 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25 were published; no new guidance, trading update or analyst action. Materially new information is not found for yesterday.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: HY26 reported 13 May 2026 growth came from volume and mix, not price: revenue AUD 3.03B, up 6.4 percent constant currency; North America installed-machine share rose to 43 percent, ANZ unit sales nearly doubled, and Product Madness recurring revenue plus iLottery content grew. Consensus models FY26 revenue down 2.6 percent on FX and portfolio effects.
web_suppliers: Not found. Aristocrat designs and assembles electronic gaming machines and licenses content, so it depends on electronics and components such as displays and chips, assembly partners, and brand licensors such as MONOPOLY. No named suppliers or evidence of supplier constraints were disclosed or found.
web_customers: Broad and not highly concentrated: land-based casinos and operators across more than 300 jurisdictions such as Yaamava' Resort and Casino, state lotteries in Massachusetts and Michigan, and online real-money operators including BetMGM through Awager. North American casino operators are the largest revenue pool.
web_who_loses: Rival suppliers losing share: Light and Wonder (ASX:LNW), IGT, Konami, Ainsworth, and social-casino rivals such as SciPlay and PlayStudios. Online content and iLottery competitors including Playtech and Evolution lose ground as Aristocrat Interactive and iLottery wins displace them.
web_contradicting_evidence: Stock closed AUD 58.40, down 2.49 percent on 2026-09-25 and about 18 percent below its 52-week high of 70.89. Consensus models FY26 revenue down 2.57 percent to AUD 6.14B and FY26 net income lower year on year than FY25. Market Index intrinsic fair value is 52.05, below the price, at roughly 24.6x earnings.
web_if_management_right: FY26 NPATA grows, 4,000 to 5,000 net new gaming units ship, and the US 1B dollar FY29 Interactive revenue target stays on track, with continued share gains in Gaming and iLottery plus buy-backs shrinking the share register. Consensus mean target AUD 66.39 implies about 14 percent upside.
web_if_management_wrong: Interactive and the US 1B dollar FY29 target slip, iLottery rollouts slow, and weak casino capex or EGM replacement demand reverses North American share gains. FX and revenue decline persist, EPS stalls and the buyback only masks it, so the roughly 24x multiple compresses.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Casino and tribal operators whose floors earn more from new cabinets; state lotteries and their platform partners; component and display suppliers; brand licensors such as Hasbro for MONOPOLY; Ainsworth via the patent licence; Awager and BetMGM for online real-slot machines; AI and analytics vendors such as Gaming Analytics.
